name: Cosmopolitan

grants.note: Choose a combat-training unarmed skill (Strikes or Grappling/Wrestling)
Distribute among Musical Composition, Writing, Drawing/Painting, Acting, Music; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among any Crafting skills (Culinary, Fabric Craft, Leathercraft, Metalcraft, Stonecraft, Woodcraft, etc.); max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute across any Lore skills (Creature, Historic, Materials, Racial, Spell, or specialization lores)
Choose from Persuasion, Intimidation, or Duping

description:
When a city gets large enough, those who dwell in it cease to be merely urban in
culture. Large cities tend to have very finely specialized craftsmen, and the
majority of their economy is devoted to trade and commerce. The combination of
specialization, access to resources and cultural experiences you only find in
large urban areas, and exposure to other people via trade and travel create a
culture that is cosmopolitan.

name: Harsh

grants.note: Choose a melee weapon skill (Blade, Hafted, etc.)
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
This culture represents people living in wastelands, though the type can vary.
Tundra, ice shelves, lava fields, true deserts, or even some form of chemically
or magically hostile wasteland all apply. People in these cultures live on the
edge of survival and tend to be very focused on survival skills applicable to
their harsh environment.

name: Highland

grants.note: Choose from Musical Composition, Writing, etc.; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
Highlanders live in rough hills or mountainous terrain. They are usually
somewhat isolated by the local geography and limited in food sources by a lack
of flat land. They tend to engage in limited agriculture and herding.

name: Mariner

grants.note: Choose from Musical Composition, Writing, etc.; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill
Choose from Persuasion, Intimidation, or Duping

description:
Mariner cultures are usually located along the shores of an ocean, lake, or
river, and their economies are usually fishing and trade based. They get the
majority of their subsistence from the water, though they may also engage in
herding or agriculture.

name: Nomad

grants.note: Choose from Musical Composition, Writing, etc.; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
Nomadic cultures tend to center around herding or hunting, driving their food
supply with them, or following its migrations. Mounts and herd animals are the
core of their lives, and they tend to be far more focused on portable property
and less focused on land ownership than non-nomads.

name: Reaver

grants.note: Choose a ranged weapon skill (Bow, Exotic Ranged, etc.)
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
Reavers represent a society of raiders, generally found in badlands adjacent to
a more settled culture. They live by preying on the productivity of others,
though they may also engage in herding or agriculture on a limited basis.

name: Rural

grants.note: Choose from Musical Composition, Writing, etc.; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill
Choose from Persuasion, Intimidation, or Duping

description:
Most of the above cultures take place in rural environments, but this culture
specifically refers to people who dwell in the rural areas of relatively open,
settled lands. Rural people are usually farmers of some sort, and tied to the
land they tend. Some rural dwellers are engaged in crafts, but they tend to be
small scale and oriented towards local use. Rural dwellers generally have a
symbiotic relationship with nearby urban dwellers, exchanging food and raw
materials for most of their manufactured goods.

name: Sylvan

grants.note: Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
Sylvan peoples are woodland dwellers who may practice some limited herding
and/or farming, but mostly live by hunting and gathering in their rich
environment. These cultures tend to be spread out with low populations, as high
concentrations of people often result in the forest being cleared and the
culture shifting to a new type.

name: Underground

grants.note: Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill

description:
People who spend most or all of their time underground or inside vast structures
are of this culture. Some steady supply of food must be available, be it animal
herds, fungus farms, or fishing, or else the culture becomes fully dependent on
trade for food (those that raid for food become Reavers).

name: Urban

grants.note: Distribute among Musical Composition, Writing, Drawing/Painting, Acting, Music; max 2 ranks/skill
Distribute among Crafting skills; max 2 ranks/skill
Choose from Persuasion, Intimidation, or Duping

description:
Urban dwellers are the people who live in the towns and small cities of a
settled area. They tend to mostly be skilled specialists or craftsmen, and
usually live a symbiotic existence with the rural people of their region,
exchanging finished goods for food and raw materials.

name: Argo
_note: Not in CoreLaw Table 2-3 — supplement culture, no standard skill grants defined

name: Hobbit
_note: Not in CoreLaw Table 2-3 — supplement culture, no standard skill grants defined

name: Oceanic
description:
Cultures whose inhabitants usually or exclusively live in the ocean, rather than simply along the coast. In Shadow World, this includes the Shuluri and Mermen.

  • Crafts: Culinary (most food will be eaten raw, but preparation is still an art), Fabric Craft (spinster, weaver), Stonecraft (stone mason). Shuluri who choose to spend at least some of their time out of the water may also develop any other craft.
  • Vocations:Hunter, shaman, healer, farmer (e.g., raising seaweed or shellfish).

name: Skulker
description:
Cultures which frequently raid other settlements, but which have limited martial might and may be subjugated or need to live in hiding. In Shadow World, these are Murlogi, Garks, and Lesser Lugroki.

  • Crafts: Culinary (cook), Leathercraft (tanner, leather worker, armorer), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith, armorer).
  • Vocations: Raider, hunter, scout, bonesetter, shaman.

name: Hunter
description:
Living in dense natural environments (forest, jungle), with some limited herding and farming but more emphasis on hunting and gathering. This culture is very similar to Sylvan (in RMU Core), but slightly more martial at the expense of lore and crafts. In Shadow World, it is typified by the Erlini.

  • Crafts: Culinary (any), Fabric Craft (any), Leathercraft (tanner, leather worker, cobbler, armorer), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith), Stonecraft (potter), Woodcraft (sawyer, carpenter, cooper, bowyer, fletcher).
  • Vocations: Hunter, farmer, scout, weaver, carpenter, leather worker.

name: Industrious
description: Hard-working Dwarves, who may not be living Underground anyway, depending on setting. Heavy emphasis on practical hard work and trade. For more martial Dwarves, the Underground culture may be more appropriate.

name: Dark
description:
Relatively powerful raider cultures more likely to subjugate others than be subjugated. In Shadow World, these are the Greater Lugroki and Trogli.

  • Crafts Culinary (cook), Leathercraft (tanner, leather worker, armorer), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith, armorer).
  • Vocations Raider, hunter, scout, bonesetter, shaman, slave master.

name: Coastal
description:
Small settlements along the ocean shore (or possibly very large lakes) foster the coastal culture. While mariner is the culture of ships and port cities, with commerce to distant lands, coastal is the culture of small fishing villages whose fishing boats do not travel far. It is rural where mariner is urban.

  • Crafts: Culinary (cook, brewer), Fabric Craft (tailor, seamstress, rope braider), Leathercraft (leather worker, armorer), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith, armorer), Woodcraft (carpenter, boat wright, cooper).
  • Vocations: Sailor, fisherman, chandler, sailmaker, rope maker.

name: Fringe
description: For those living on the fringes of urban society. Intended for the avinarc, but could also be suitable for goblins and such existing as underclass and criminally-adjacent night-folk in the cities of humans or similar types. This gives Survival (urban), the RMU version of streetwise and a bit of subterfuge, while cutting down a little on the entertainment and gainful employment skills.

name: Noble
description:
Born into privilege, those of noble birth are raised in a unique environment. They are provided with the best education possible, expected to master social etiquette, and exposed to the arts; they are free from the obligation to learn a trade and engage in rote labor. This culture could encompass the children of the most favored servants, but most lower-class members of noble households will be of the urban or other cultures. This culture is most appropriate in urban areas. Smaller social groups tend to be more egalitarian and the children of leaders will be raised much like any other child.

  • Crafts: Noble crafts will tend to be artistic rather than mundane, or immediately related to their martial duties. Drawing/Painting, Fabric Craft (spinster, weaver, seamstress), Leathercraft (armorer), Metalcraft (gold smith, jeweler, silver smith, weapon smith, armorer), Stonecraft (sculptor), Woodcraft (carpenter, bowyer).
  • Vocations: Knight, squire, court noble, adviser, landowner.

name: Proud
description:
Placing a high value on honor, this culture is quick to go to war when they believe there is a noble cause. They may take offense easily in which case this is a frequent occurrence, but in any case they see battle as an opportunity to earn status. This may be a relatively egalitarian culture in which everyone is expected to farm in peaceful times and fight in times of war, or this may be the ruling class, in which case the peasantry may be better characterized by the Rural (farming) or Highland (herding) cultures. In Shadow World, this may be an appropriate choice for the Jaaderi, Laan, and Talath.

  • Crafts: Culinary (any), Fabric Craft (any), Leathercraft (any), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith, armorer), Stonecraft (mason, stone dresser, potter), Woodcraft (sawyer, carpenter, cart wright, cooper).
  • Vocations: Herdsman, farmer, weaver, stonemason, carpenter, soldier, militia, miner.

name: Ascended
description:
These cultures have a connection to nature but nevertheless are city builders and craftsmen rather than living a sylvan lifestyle. They are also more familiar with magic than other cultures. In Shadow World, this includes the Loari, Linaeri, and Dyari elves, as well as the Jhordi.

  • Crafts: Ascended cultures encourage specialization and appreciate a wide range of crafts. Any craft is appropriate.
  • Vocations: Bookkeeper, guardsman, librarian, manager, merchant, officer, scribe, soldier, valet, or any type of craftsman. Due to their familiarity with magic, magic-oriented vocations may also be possible, such as magical researchers, healers, and alchemists.

name: Singer
description: The artistic and peaceful Nycamerith. Because they are racially non-violent (2 tiers as a Flaw), I did not give them a rank of Unarmed combat training. Instead, they are rich in artistic and crafting skills, as well as learning a great deal of language from the songs they have shared. Their preference for avoiding dangers leads to having all the Movement skills.

name: Hermit
description: The unique lifestyle of the Gnomes.

name: Aerial
description:
Living high in the mountains, unanchored from the earth, winged races are not freed from the need to eke out a living and gather or raise food. However, they make more use of domesticated animals than Harsh cultures, and are more inclined to find and follow prey from the air than to track it along the ground. This culture typifies the Hirzi.

  • Crafts: Aerial cultures need physical goods and build shelters just as earthbound cultures. Their needs are much like those of highland cultures, except they are less likely to accept the encumbrance of heavier armors, and due to living in the most difficult terrain may not make much use of carts and wagons. Culinary (cook, brewer, butcher), Fabric Craft (any), Leathercraft (any), Metalcraft (blacksmith, weapon smith), Stonecraft (mason, stone dresser, potter), Woodcraft (sawyer, carpenter, cooper).
  • Vocations: Herdsman, farmer, hunter, weaver, stonemason, carpenter, soldier.

name: Secret Nomad
description: The cautious, mobile-at-need Gnolls. The Lore skill should be Creature Lore: Elementals.

name: Sanctified
description:
Some societies have a well-established religious caste. Those born into this class are raised from birth to become priests and priestesses. Like nobles, they may be largely free from the need to learn a trade, but expected to learn the dogma and practices of their faith, as well as its formalized ceremonies. They may learn arts that glorify the divine, and they will generally be well-educated. Not all members of the clergy will be of this culture; depending on the society, priests may be recruited from all backgrounds. Members of this culture are specifically those individuals who spent their formative years within the temple or church.

  • Crafts: Some religions may practice only crafts deemed to honor their faith, but others may see constructive work as useful in developing discipline. (Although note that faiths which expect full participation in regular society may not be appropriate for the Sanctified culture.) Culinary (any), Drawing/Painting, Fabric Craft (any), Metalcraft (any), Stonecraft (any), Woodcraft (carpenter, cooper).
  • Vocations: Priest, acolyte, singer, musician, dancer, teacher, scribe.

name: Sea-Raider
description: For the Sea-Krals. They are good at messing about in boats, but cannot swim. They have that Reaver savagery, but have much less use for animal skills, especially Riding, while Tracking is not all that practical at sea.

name: Ritualist
description: The lifestyle of the Sstoi'isslythi, who are able to focus less on gaining food (with a cold-blooded appetite) and maintain strong, complex traditions.
